subject.title: [Bug]: cron.remove does not clean up session records in sessions.json

question: Should deleted cron jobs purge their base session record immediately on `cron.remove`, or should orphaned base sessions be cleaned later through `cron.sessionRetention`?
rationale: Current source leaves base cron session rows untouched, while linked retention work needs to preserve live base rows that may carry model/auth/label state; choosing immediate deletion versus retention-based cleanup needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Ownership-aware immediate purge
options.body: Make `cron.remove` remove only the deleted job's owned session artifacts and obsolete run history, with tests proving active jobs' base rows are preserved.

options.title: Repair linked retention PR
options.body: Use the broader retention PR as the landing path if maintainers accept retention-delayed cleanup for deleted jobs and repair its conflicts.

options.title: Retention-only cleanup later
options.body: Keep `cron.remove` limited to job config and rely on a future reaper change to prune stale orphaned base rows after the configured retention window.

recommendation.title: Ownership-aware immediate purge
recommendation.body: Make `cron.remove` remove only the deleted job's owned session artifacts and obsolete run history, with tests proving active jobs' base rows are preserved.

likelyOwner.reason: The relevant lifecycle choice sits closest to the session maintenance and cron pruning contract that gumadeiras introduced and hardened.
